newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Four Nigerian firms bid for oil leases - reports.
newsitem.headline: Four Nigerian firms bid for oil leases - reports.

text.p: Four Nigerian oil firms have applied for oil prospecting leases in a growing rush of applications, local newspapers reported on Tuesday.
This brings to 22 local and foreign firms seeking to participate in oil exploration in Nigeria in the past seven months.
The independent Guardian newspaper said the latest bidders were Royal Petroleum Services, Pabod Petroleum Development Company, Macs Investment Limited and George-Donia Oil and Engineering Services.
The four are bidding for a total of 18 acreages.
The bids, submitted in February to the Department of Petroleum Resources, bring to 54 the number of oil mining leases being sought by oil firms new to the industry in Nigeria since last October.

Industry sources said the latest bids were an indication that local firms were still keen to participate in exploration activities, although only two out of 24 such firms granted oil mining leases between 1991 and 1993 have started production and export.
Amni produces 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) while Consolidated Oil's output is 7,000 bpd.
The rest of Nigeria's roughly two million bpd output is produced by foreign firms, mostly in joint venture arrangements with state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp.
